title: India Open U19 Women's World Cup Defence Against West Indies in Kathmandu
excerpt: Two-time defending champions India face West Indies on January 22, 2027, in Kirtipur, with Nepal and Ireland completing Group A in the 16-team tournament hosted by Bangladesh and Nepal.
body:
• Defending champions India open their ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2027 campaign against West Indies on January 22, 2027, at the TU International Cricket Stadium in Kirtipur, Kathmandu.
  • India are in Group A with West Indies, hosts Nepal and Ireland, and play all three group matches in Kathmandu: West Indies on January 22, Nepal on January 24 and Ireland on January 26.
  • The tournament runs January 21 to February 6, 2027, in Bangladesh and Nepal, with 16 teams, 41 matches, four venues, a Super Six stage, semi-finals on February 4 and the final in Chattogram on February 6.
  • India have won both previous editions — beating England in 2023 and South Africa by nine wickets in the 2025 final — and are chasing a third successive title.

India will begin the defence of their ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup title against West Indies in Kathmandu on January 22, 2027, after the ICC announced the schedule for the third edition of the tournament. The BCCI confirmed that the two-time defending champions have been drawn in Group A alongside West Indies, hosts Nepal and Ireland, with all three of India's group matches at the TU International Cricket Stadium in Kathmandu.

India's Group Fixtures

India face West Indies on January 22, Nepal on January 24 and Ireland on January 26, all in Kathmandu. The top three teams from each group progress to the Super Six stage, so a single defeat in the group does not end a campaign, but seeding from the group stage carries into the Super Six and can shape the semi-final path.

https://x.com/cricbuzz/status/2112798366044508429

The other groups underline the breadth of the 16-team field. Group B contains 2025 runners-up South Africa, New Zealand, Pakistan and Samoa. Group C contains Australia, co-hosts Bangladesh, Nigeria and the United Arab Emirates. Group D contains England, Sri Lanka, the United States and Scotland, according to ESPNcricinfo. India and Pakistan have been placed in separate groups.

Tournament Format and Venues

The tournament will be held from January 21 to February 6, 2027, across four venues in Bangladesh and Nepal: Chattogram and Sylhet in Bangladesh, and Kirtipur and Mulpani in Nepal. All 41 matches will be played during the day, with morning games starting at 9:30am local time and afternoon games at 1:30pm local time.

The competition opens with four matches on January 21: Bangladesh against UAE and Australia against Nigeria in Sylhet, and Sri Lanka against Scotland and England against USA in Mulpani. The remaining eight teams start on January 22, including New Zealand against Samoa and South Africa against Pakistan in Chattogram, and Nepal against Ireland alongside India against West Indies in Kirtipur. After the group stage, the Super Six splits qualifiers into two groups, with the top two from each reaching the semi-finals on February 4 in Chattogram. The final follows in Chattogram on February 6, with reserve days allotted for both the semi-finals and the final.

"The ICC U19 World Cup is the stage that showcases the future of our sport and serves as the ultimate platform for young players to make the leap towards elite careers representing their countries."

— Sanjog Gupta, ICC CEO

Chasing a Three-Peat

India have won both editions held so far, defeating England in the inaugural tournament in 2023 and then defending the title in 2025 with a nine-wicket win over South Africa in the final. No other team has lifted the trophy. That record makes India the team to beat, but it also means a largely new cohort must carry the expectation: U19 squads turn over quickly, and the players who won in 2025 will mostly have aged out by January 2027.

The choice of Bangladesh and Nepal as co-hosts is part of the story. The ICC said the hosts reflect its investment in the future of the cricket ecosystem, noting the deep passion for cricket in both countries and that nearly 40 percent of their populations are below the age of 20. For Nepal, staging India's group matches in Kirtipur is a significant home tournament, and the January 24 Nepal against India fixture is likely to be one of the best-attended group games.

What to Watch

Squad announcements, warm-up fixtures and broadcast details are still to come. For diaspora viewers in the United States, the daytime starts in Nepal and Bangladesh translate to late-night viewing the previous evening, so the January 22 opener against West Indies, a 1:30pm local start in Kathmandu, will fall in the early hours of the morning in US time zones. The first test of India's title defence is now fixed; the squad that attempts the three-peat is the next piece of news to watch.
